title: Holy Cross Day (14 September)
hookLine: the cross honored as a sign of victory, not only suffering

lines: ONE DAY FOR THE CROSS ITSELF.
cards: "God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." Paul wrote that to the churches in Galatia: a strange sentence. Glory, in a cross.
In Paul's world, a cross was how Rome put people to death, and the letter to the Hebrews speaks of its shame. Not a thing to boast in.

And yet people now trace it on their foreheads, raise it over altars, and hang it round their necks. One day in the church year honors the cross itself, not as a defeat but as a victory. Today, Holy Cross Day.

teach.b: Good Friday looks at the cross with grief. Holy Cross Day looks at it with something closer to wonder.
Orthodox Christians call it the Exaltation, or the Elevation, of the Cross: a cross is lifted high, and people bow before it. Catholics and some Protestant churches keep the day too.

The story behind it is a tradition, not scripture: tradition says that Helena, the mother of the emperor Constantine, searched in Jerusalem for the cross of Jesus, and that a church was built at the place.
But the Bible gives the feast its turn of thought. In John, Jesus says, "And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me." Lifted up: execution and exaltation at once.
Peter's first letter says Jesus "bare our sins in his own body on the tree." A tree.

That word sends some readers back to the garden, where Genesis places "the tree of life also in the midst of the garden," and forward to Revelation, where the tree of life stands again by a river, and "the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations."
Old hymns and sermons sing of the cross as a tree: dead wood become the tree of life.

teach.h: A TREE AT THE START AND THE END.
teach.b: A tree in a garden at the start, a tree on a hill in the middle, a tree by a river at the end. That's why the day can be joyful. Christians don't forget the suffering.
They honor the cross as the place where, they say, death lost.

how: On Holy Cross Day, Orthodox churches lift up a cross for the faithful to venerate, and Catholic and some Protestant churches read the scriptures of the cross; Christians in several traditions mark themselves with the sign of the cross in prayer.

games.q: you're reading Revelation's last pages. there's a river, and beside it a tree. what does the text say its leaves are for?

for the healing of the nations.

games.why: the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. Christians hear the tree of life from Genesis come back at the end.

practice: If it's part of your practice, trace the cross slowly, forehead, chest, shoulder to shoulder, the way your church does; if not, simply bow your head, as people bow before the lifted cross.
Then hold one thing in your life that feels like dead wood, and let a tree with healing leaves sit beside it.

wordCard.voice: Exaltation. The name Orthodox Christians give the feast that honors the cross as a sign of victory, the dead wood they call the tree of life.

orig.note: Greek: wood, a tree. the word on the tree in Peter's letter, and in the tree of life in Revelation.

carryVoice: Your line: the tree of life. It closes a week of feasts, from John's birth to the cross. Go gently.
